correctness.rationale: Strict convexity for all feasible gain vectors implies unique global optimum. Graph automorphisms imply orbitwise common peripheral gain. A spectral decomposition produces the scalar rational trace and boundary derivative \(P_m(B/(2m))/B\). A globally positive quartic bound excludes hub deletion for \(m\le8\). For \(m\ge9\), an exact negative sign witness plus Descartes\' rule on at most two positive roots gives precisely two switching budgets, and scaling limits give \(B_-(m)/m\to4/3\) and \(B_+(m)/m^2\to2\). Symbolic and full-matrix numerical checks reproduce the nonstandard calculations; no finite check is used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: The free-gain support of the highest-degree hub is a motivated control-resource question. A sharp graph-size boundary (8 versus 9), complete two-threshold classification of all budgets, unique unrestricted optimizers and distinct linear/quadratic transition scales give structural information beyond reusing convexity or checking a small graph. This network also separates optimizing gains from selecting finitely many leaders.
